nodes.content: Recover relightable geometry and materials from three images under unknown illumination while quantifying ambiguity between shape, reflectance, and lighting.
requirements: Reduce held-out relighting LPIPS by 15% versus a matched point-estimate inverse renderer.
Achieve 85–95% coverage for nominal 90% predictive intervals on held-out relighting intensities.

nodes.content: Fit a gauge-normalized mesh–BRDF–lighting posterior with diffusion priors; select LPIPS-medoid relightings and conformally calibrate intensity intervals.
Does gauge normalization preserve shape–lighting ambiguity sufficiently for calibrated intensity intervals under unseen directional lights?
Energy normalization with free exposure preserves shape–lighting modes, yielding 85–95% coverage for 90% intervals under unseen directional lights.
On TriLight-Objects, compare free versus fixed exposure using three-image posteriors; measure directional-relighting coverage and shape–light correlations.
Run a TriLight-Objects ablation on 120 objects, fitting free- and fixed-exposure posteriors; measure 90% interval coverage and shape–light correlations.
On TriLight-Objects, free versus fixed exposure yielded 91% versus 78% 90%-interval coverage; median absolute shape–light correlations were 0.58 versus 0.21.
Retain free exposure with energy normalization because it achieved 91% coverage and preserved stronger shape–light correlations than fixed exposure.
Benchmark free-exposure posterior medoids against a matched point-estimate renderer on TriLight-Objects unseen lights; measure LPIPS reduction and 90%-interval coverage.
TriLight-Objects benchmark package containing held-out relightings, posterior-versus-point-estimate LPIPS comparisons, 90% intensity intervals, coverage tables, and evaluation scripts.
Ablate diffusion priors and conformal calibration across free- and fixed-exposure TriLight-Objects fits; measure directional-light LPIPS, coverage, shape–light correlations.
TriLight-Objects: medoid LPIPS was 0.198 versus 0.220 without priors and 0.240 point-estimate; calibration raised free-exposure coverage 82%→91%.
Free-exposure joint shape–light samples retain ≥85% interval coverage beyond 60° from training lights; independently shuffled samples do not.
Stratify TriLight-Objects relightings beyond 60°; compare 90% interval coverage from joint versus shape–light-shuffled posterior samples with calibration fixed.
Beyond 60°, joint posterior coverage fell to 81% versus 74% shuffled, refuting the predicted ≥85% despite preserved dependence.
On TriLight-Objects, compare joint and shuffled 90% interval coverage separately for cast-shadow and lit pixels beyond 60°.
With shadow-stratified calibration, joint coverage beyond 60° reached 87% in shadows and 90% lit; shuffled reached 77% and 82%.
Fit a shadow-aware neural SDF mixture with coupled BRDF–lighting modes, perceptual-risk relighting, and shadow-stratified intensity calibration.
Can a shadow-aware SDF mixture distinguish cast-shadow uncertainty from dark albedo while improving unseen-light relighting LPIPS?
Shadow-aware SDF modes achieve shadow-versus-albedo AUROC ≥0.85 and unseen-light LPIPS ≤0.185, versus 0.198 for p1.
Train shadow-aware SDF mixtures from three TriLight-Objects views; evaluate shadow–albedo AUROC on labeled pixels and held-out LPIPS against p1.
Train p2 on 120 TriLight-Objects using three views; score labeled shadow–albedo AUROC and unseen-light LPIPS against p1.
On TriLight-Objects, p2 achieved shadow–albedo AUROC 0.88 and unseen-light LPIPS 0.181, versus p1’s 0.198.
Advance p2 to interval-calibration testing: AUROC reached 0.88 and unseen-light LPIPS fell to 0.181 versus p1’s 0.198.
Evaluate p2’s shadow-stratified 90% intervals on held-out TriLight-Objects lights; check 85–95% coverage and LPIPS against the 0.240 baseline.
TriLight-Objects p2 evaluation report with shadow-stratified coverage, held-out LPIPS versus the 0.240 baseline, calibration splits, and reproducible scripts.
Use parallel-tempered path-tracing MCMC to sample geometry–BRDF–lighting modes from three views, then select perceptual-risk relightings and calibrate intensity intervals.
Parallel-tempered path tracing reduces held-out TriLight-Objects LPIPS from 0.240 to ≤0.200 while maintaining 85–95% coverage for 90% intervals.
Run eight-chain tempered path-tracing MCMC on TriLight-Objects; measure held-out LPIPS against 0.240 and calibrated 90% interval coverage.
Tempered MCMC achieved LPIPS 0.215 versus 0.240 baseline, missing ≤0.200, despite 89% coverage for 90% intervals.
Stratify tempered-MCMC relightings by specularity and shadow area; measure LPIPS, interval coverage, and geometry–lighting mode-mixing diagnostics.
On low-specularity, low-shadow objects, tempered MCMC achieved LPIPS 0.192 and 91% interval coverage, supporting n24 only in this subset.
Does poor mixing between specular BRDF and lighting modes explain p3’s LPIPS 0.215 outside the low-specularity subset?
Compare BRDF–lighting swap moves against standard MCMC on specular TriLight-Objects; measure cross-mode ESS and LPIPS versus low-specularity objects.
Implement joint BRDF–lighting swap moves on TriLight-Objects; compare cross-mode ESS and LPIPS against original chains across specular and low-specularity objects.
Tempered-MCMC swap-move implementation with reproducible TriLight-Objects chain traces, specularity labels, cross-mode ESS calculations, and held-out LPIPS scripts.
Train a 16-particle inverse renderer with coupled mesh–BRDF–lighting hypotheses, relighting-space diversity, perceptual-risk selection, and shadow-stratified conformal intervals.
Do relighting-space diversity penalties prevent particle collapse across specular BRDF–lighting modes without degrading 90% interval coverage?
Relighting-space repulsion doubles distinct specular modes among 16 particles while maintaining 85–95% coverage for calibrated 90% intervals.
Ablate relighting-space repulsion in 16-particle TriLight-Objects fits; count distinct specular modes and measure calibrated 90% interval coverage.
On TriLight-Objects, repulsion raised median distinct specular modes from 3 to 7; calibrated 90% intervals retained 90% coverage.
Keep relighting-space repulsion in p4: it increased distinct specular modes from 3 to 7 with 90% interval coverage.
Stratify p4’s repulsive-particle results by specularity and unseen-light angle; compare mode counts, LPIPS, and interval coverage against no repulsion.
TriLight-Objects p4 stratification report with specularity- and angle-binned mode counts, LPIPS, 90% coverage, and repulsion-ablation plots.
Train a triplet-conditioned shape–BRDF–lighting flow; importance-reweight samples by path-traced likelihoods and calibrate shadow-stratified relighting intervals.
Train the triplet-conditioned flow on TriLight-Objects; importance-reweight 256 samples per object, then benchmark LPIPS against 0.240 and shadow-stratified 90% coverage.
Benchmark 256 reweighted p5 samples with shadow calibration; audit n39 by independently reproducing its stratified LPIPS and coverage.
On TriLight-Objects, reweighted p5 achieved LPIPS 0.196 versus 0.240 baseline and 91% interval coverage; n39’s stratified trends reproduced.
On specular TriLight-Objects, compare p5’s reweighted samples against n32 swap-move chains for mode recall, weight ESS, LPIPS, and 90%-interval coverage.
On specular TriLight-Objects, p5 recovered 6/8 modes versus swap chains’ 4/8; LPIPS was 0.203 versus 0.218, with 89% coverage.
Advance p5: LPIPS reached 0.196 versus 0.240 with 91% coverage; specular mode recall was 6/8 versus swap chains’ 4/8.
Validate p5 on disjoint objects under unseen HDR lights; require ≥15% LPIPS improvement versus matched baseline and 85–95% 90%-interval coverage.
TriLight-Objects HDR validation bundle with disjoint-object splits, unseen-light renders, matched-baseline LPIPS, 90%-interval coverage, importance weights, and evaluation scripts.
